title: Leningrad Cut Off
subtitle: The opening of the Leningrad blockade
author: R.G. Cruise
phase: III — The Battle for Strategic Objectives
summary: Shlisselburg’s capture severed the principal overland connection to Leningrad; Lake Ladoga remained a route across the water.
location: Leningrad, Lake Ladoga and the Neva
outlineTopics: Leningrad's political, industrial, and strategic importance.
Army Group North's advance during August and early September.
German 4th Panzer Group and the infantry armies involved.
Soviet defensive preparations around the city.
The Luga defensive system and subsequent fighting.
The role of Soviet forces defending the southern approaches.
The German capture of Shlisselburg on September 8.
The severing of Leningrad's principal overland connection with the Soviet interior.
The continuing importance of Lake Ladoga.
Finnish military positions north of Leningrad.
The relationship between Finnish operations and the German blockade.
German intentions toward the population of Leningrad.
German starvation policy and the decision not to rely on a conventional occupation of the city.
The immediate consequences for civilians, food supplies, transportation, and evacuation.
The distinction between the blockade's beginning and the much longer siege that followed.
researchStatus: Editorial outline and date association established. Full researched narrative, claim-level citations and the dated military situation remain to be written and reconstructed.
referenceMapStatus: Candidate German General Staff plate from the supplied chronological sequence. The plate title/date, operational content and reuse conditions have not been independently verified for digitisation.
chronologyNotes: 8 September began the land blockade, not the later winter catastrophe. Leningrad remained in Soviet hands and Lake Ladoga was not closed.
